$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the half of the coverage rule the other cases do not reach. The gate
block declares all four domains and the document assesses three, so the fourth is declared and never audited.
Coverage counts a domain only when both halves carry it, and this is the case that holds that second half:
reading the gate alone would score this report 4 of 4.
It is also the case that shows what the disagreement count deliberately does not do. Maintainability is
answered in one place and not the other, which is an incomplete deliverable rather than a contradiction, so
gateDisagreements stays empty and coverage is what reports it.
It is gapped-correct-audit with the `## Maintainability Assessment` section deleted and its gate line kept.
The report is CONSTRUCTED, following nfr-report-template.md's section order and its Gate YAML snippet.
derivation: Gate block: security PASS, performance CONCERNS, reliability FAIL, maintainability CONCERNS.
Sections: security PASS, performance CONCERNS, reliability FAIL, and no maintainability section at all.
Maintainability is declared and unassessed, so it is not present: coverage 3 of 4 against 3 headings. Its
status is still the gate's CONCERNS, which matches the corpus, so there is no status miss.
Gate disagreements: none. Only a domain both halves answer can contradict.
The maintainability citations and the Test Coverage evidence gap went with the deleted section, so the
citation map carries three domains and the gaps list is empty. Overall, thresholds elsewhere, and the
Grounding: all 15 of 15 criteria with declared evidence cite the file ground truth declares for
them; none is ungrounded. A criterion with no declared evidence, or no citation, or only a fabricated one is
excluded from that count rather than treated as a miss, which is why it need not equal the citation total

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
